entries.title: Cause found: button wire on GPIO 4
entries.why: The photo showed the ESP32 sits in a screw-terminal expansion board, not in the breadboard, so the guide's “breadboard row” instructions did not apply. The GND wire was right; the signal wire was in socket 4, next to 5.

entries.title: W2 unreachable: diagnosis
entries.where: Board · network + serial · with your go
entries.cmd: ping -c 3 192.168.178.54 && curl -s -m 5 http://192.168.178.54/api/status && uv run python tools/read_serial.py /dev/cu.usbserial-A5069RR4 15
entries.why: W2 joined your Wi-Fi (teal dot, IP 192.168.178.54) but phone and Mac said “unreachable”. The Mac is on the same network and the firmware file contains the web server.
entries.out:
ping: 0 of 3 answered
curl: timeout, then couldn't connect
bench.local -> 192.168.178.54 (mDNS got through)
[ 13233] scan 1 done: 10 networks in 3227 ms
[ 13298] scan started (auto)   <- 65 ms later, should be 10 s
entries.result: Bug: the clock was read before the scan check, so `now - finishedAt` wrapped around and the board scanned non-stop, taking its radio off your router's channel. Fixed (60 s between scans once joined); not flashed yet. Opening the serial port also restarted the board once (FTDI on macOS).

entries.where: Board flashed by you · checks on the Mac only

ping -c 3 192.168.178.54 && arp -n 192.168.178.54 && curl -s -m 5 http://192.168.178.54/api/status && dns-sd -G v4 bench.local   (Claude, Mac only)
entries.why: The scan fix works (next auto-scan 60 s later, not 65 ms), but phone and Mac still couldn't open the page. The Mac checks don't touch the USB port.
entries.out:
Connected to 'FRITZ!Box 5530 GK': IP 192.168.178.54, channel 11, -54 dBm
E mdns_responder: Service already exists

Mac 192.168.178.31 on en0 (5 GHz ch 116), same network, no VPN
ping: 0 of 3 answered
arp 192.168.178.54: (incomplete)   <- no answer to “who has .54?”
curl: exit 7, couldn't connect
bench.local: answered from the Mac's cache (flag 0x40000000)
entries.result: Below the web server: the board doesn't even answer ARP. Built, not flashed: Wi-Fi power save off once joined (known FRITZ!Box issue), mDNS started once, and a serial `ping` / `ping <ip>` to test from the board's side. Router check: FRITZ!Box → WLAN → Security → “WLAN devices may communicate with each other” must be ticked.

entries.title: Cause found: the router isolates Wi-Fi devices
entries.where: Board flashed + serial ping by you · checks on the Mac only
entries.cmd:
uv run pio run -e wifi-lab -t upload   (you)
ping  ·  ping 192.168.178.31   (you, in the serial monitor)
ping/arp/curl to .54 + socketfilterfw --getglobalstate --getstealthmode   (Claude, Mac only)
entries.why: With power save off, test the network from both ends to see which link is broken.
entries.out:
board -> router  192.168.178.1:  4 sent, 4 answered (1-2 ms)
board -> Mac    192.168.178.31: 3 sent, 0 answered, send error=0 (no ARP answer)
Mac -> board: ping 0 of 3, arp (incomplete), curl exit 7
Mac firewall: disabled, stealth mode off
entries.result: Board and Mac both reach the router, but not each other, and the Mac firewall is off: the FRITZ!Box doesn't pass traffic between Wi-Fi devices. Fix: fritz.box → WLAN → Security → tick “WLAN devices may communicate with each other”. Workaround: serial `setup`, join bench-setup, open http://192.168.4.1.

entries.title: Reboot + reflash: screen lit but blank
entries.where: Board flashed by you · status read over Wi-Fi by Claude (no USB)
entries.cmd:
uv run pio run -e wifi-lab -t upload   (you)
curl -s -m 5 http://192.168.178.54/api/status   (Claude)
entries.why: After Reboot in the app and a reflash, the backlight is on but nothing is drawn. The monitor shows Wi-Fi messages, so the firmware runs past the screen set-up.
entries.out: /api/status -> {"endpoints": ["GET /api/status", ...]}   <- the API index, not the status
entries.result: Separate firmware bug: a plain "/api" route also matched every /api/... GET, so status and networks returned the index (PUT/POST fine, so Reboot worked). Fixed with exact matches, built, not flashed. Screen: likely a loose data wire (pins 12/11/10/9/8) or a panel that needs a real power cycle.

entries.title: rfid-lab on the board: an FM17522 clone, and a chip that went quiet
entries.where: board · flashed and read by you
entries.cmd:
uv run pio run -e rfid-lab -t upload   (by you)
uv run pio device monitor: chip · chip · selftest
uv run pio run -e rfid-lab   (the fix, Mac only)
entries.why: Your first R1 run. The reader chip answered B2h: an FM17522 clone, not an NXP MFRC522, so the datasheet's self-test table can't apply to it. Then, after the card was moved, the chip stopped answering: the self-test read VersionReg 00h before it even started.
entries.out:
00:17:08  VersionReg 0xB2: FM17522 (clone)
00:17:59  VersionReg 0xB2: FM17522 (clone)
00:17:56  unknown command 'chip'   (a backspace inside the line)
00:18:22  card removed
00:18:32  Self-test, chip 0x00, FIFO level 0: 64 × 00
          self-test: no reference for chip 0x00 (a clone)
fix build: rfid-lab  Flash 6.7% (438,307 B)  SUCCESS, no warnings
entries.result: Likely a header pin losing contact while the card was handled. Fixed in the firmware (built, not flashed): a 2 s VersionReg watchdog that hard-resets a silent chip and says hang or wire, a reset command, a self-test that refuses a silent chip and compares two runs on clones, and backspace in serial input.

entries.title: R7 on your board: unreliable reads, EPIPE, UI pass
entries.cmd:
uv run pio run -e rfid-lab-r1 … -e rfid-lab-r7   (build only)
door-app: tsc · vitest · vite + mock board, headless Chromium
entries.why: You saw the app live with the time, but a card “can't be read”, the LED red then off, and Vite printing “ws proxy error: EPIPE”. Compared with R1-R6 (which work on your board), R7 never fell back from the IRQ wire to polling, and its health check only read VersionReg, which survives a 3.3 V dip that resets the chip's other settings (antenna off). Fixes: IRQ fallback after every poll; a settings check every 2 s that restores them; jobs try the card 3 times; failure messages say why (no card / chip silent / garbled answer); the status reports reader health, uptime and the last restart's reason (crash, brownout). EPIPE: React's development double start closed a socket mid-handshake; the app now lets it open first. UI: a status bar, a problem banner, an “On the reader” slot with Read it / Save its data, the log under the door, tidier card rows.
entries.out:
rfid-lab-r1 … r7  SUCCESS, no warnings · r7 RAM 17.0%  Flash 18.1%
door-app: typecheck clean · 10 tests passed · no page errors, no sideways scroll, no proxy errors
entries.result: Next, by you: uv run pio run -e rfid-lab-r7 -t upload, then watch the Reader chip cell and the banner while you tap. If it still fails, paste the serial lines (or say go and Claude reads the port). Nothing was sent to the board.

entries.title: R7 works; card names shown as JSON, loading states
entries.cmd:
c++ -std=c++17 … ajtest/main.cpp   (Mac only: ArduinoJson 7.4.3 check)
uv run pio run -e rfid-lab-r7   (build only)
door-app: tsc · vitest · vite + slow mock board, headless Chromium
entries.why: R7 reads now, also with the card a little above the reader. Your Reader chip cell said “polling · settings restored 5× · lost 5×”: the IRQ wire stays quiet (so polling), and a 3.3 V dip reset the RC522 5 times, each time put right within 2 s. The supply still dips, so short 3.3V wires and pressed-in headers are worth it. New bug: a card's name, then a snapshot's, showed a piece of JSON. ArduinoJson 7.4 treats any const char[N] as a string literal and keeps only its pointer; the Card copy was gone by the time the JSON was sent, and the memory held the previous card's JSON. Fix: char-array fields go through doorjson::copied() (a const char *, which is copied). Nothing stored was damaged. App: grey placeholders until the list, saved data and log arrive; a turning ring with a “doing” label on every button that waits for the board.
entries.out:
before: [{"name":"########################…"}]  after: [{"name":"abdu"},{"name":"card"}]
rfid-lab-r7 SUCCESS, no warnings · RAM 17.0%  Flash 18.1%

entries.title: R7: an admin room only admin cards open
entries.cmd:
c++ -std=c++17 -Wall -I src/rfid-lab-r7 test/host/door_rules_test.cpp   (Mac only)
uv run pio run -e rfid-lab-r7   (build only)
door-app: tsc · vitest · vite + mock board, headless Chromium
entries.why: You asked for another lock that admins open and residents don't. New role: admin (stored as the next role byte, so your card list stays). Two locks: Front door (every role, as before) and Admin room. New rule right after “blocked”: at the admin room, anything but an admin card → DENIED · admins only. Admins also open during lockdown. The bench has one reader, so it is mounted at one lock at a time: Move reader here in the app, or serial at front|admin (saved on the board). Each lock has its own OPEN / DENIED / LOCKED and its own Open 5 s (POST /api/open?lock=admin). Cards show what a tap would do at each lock; the log says which lock. The guide's rule panel has the new rule; the bench simulator still shows one door.

entries.why: You asked for a Bluetooth lab going from reading to pairing to controlling, with the phone, peripherals like sound or a keyboard, and creative examples, one lab per step. The ESP32-S3 has Bluetooth LE only, so it can't stream audio to your JBL; it controls the phone that does (B6) or plays MIDI notes a synth turns into sound (B7). Eight labs on a shared lib/ble-kit: B1 Listen, B2 Be seen, B3 Connect & talk, B4 Pair & trust, B5 Phone app (+ test-esp/ble-app, Web Bluetooth), B6 Keyboard & media, B7 Music (BLE-MIDI), B8 Host (your keyboard and mouse on the board).
